title: Regional cutover conductor and incremental snapshot rehydration protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operationally deterministic playbook and automation suite for active-passive regional cutovers that uses incremental snapshot rehydration to minimize RPO while preserving latency SLOs. This ticket covers the conductor runbook (human + automation steps), SLO/alert gates for promotion/demotion, circuit breaker and load-shedding knobs to apply during ramp, and validation harness for backup/restore correctness. Aim is to provide a single-run procedure that non-oncall site reliability engineers can execute during scheduled drills and emergency failovers.
runbook_steps: Pre-cutover validation: confirm primary region tokenstore WAL lag < 30s and KV replica lag < 5s; run quick consistency-check job (sha256 checksums of top-100k keys) and snapshot TTL < 2m; fail if mismatch > 0.1%
Snapshot staging: create incremental snapshot (snap-incr) and store to s3://redwood-dr/snapshots/<timestamp>; ensure snapshot manifest written and checksum validated
Fence and quiesce primary: apply per-service fencing policy (circuit-breaker drain for 60s, stop leader election, mark region as read-only) via orchestrator API; confirm no write leases remain
Promote passive: trigger conductor to stream-incremental snapshot to passive region nodes, apply write-enabled flag only after KV index reconciliation + checksum pass
Traffic cutover in waves: shift 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 10-minute observation windows and SLO gates at each step

Post-cutover verification: run data integrity audit (key counts, top-k ratio, request-response checksum sampling), validate latency SLOs on 50th/95th/99th percentiles, validate token issuance and auth path

Rollback criteria & steps: if error rate spike above threshold or core SLOs breached for two consecutive windows, revert traffic to old region and start rehydration rollback (preserve new writes in buffer), then open incident and run postmortem
Post-mortem checklist: capture snapshots of prometheus metrics, tracing spans for cutover window, and conductor logs; schedule blameless postmortem and remediation PRs
sla_gates: Pre-cutover: KV replica lag < 5s; tokenstore WAL age < 30s
Wave gates: 95th-percentile latency <= 2x baseline AND error-rate delta < 0.25% for the observation window
Final gate: 99th-percentile latency not degraded by >300ms and user-facing errors <= 0.5% above baseline
metrics_thresholds: Error-rate delta: >0.5% sustained over two windows triggers rollback
P95 latency: >2x baseline sustained over one window triggers circuit-breaker for non-critical routes
KV-consistency-failures: any non-zero count forces abort of promotion
circuit_breaker_and_load_shedding: Primary CBs: global per-route circuit breaker with fast-open on error-rate >0.8% and slow-open if latency P99 > 3s
Load-shedding policy: tiered degrade — 1) disable background low-priority jobs, 2) reject or queue long-running admin operations, 3) enable token TTL short-circuiting for analytics clients
Graceful degradation: apply feature flag to divert low-priority traffic to degraded model variant or cached responses during ramp windows
validation_harness_and_tests: Automated restore job: k8s job that rehydrates incremental snapshot into isolated test cluster and runs end-to-end smoke tests
Checksum test: nightly job that compares sample key checksums between primary and passive with failure threshold 0.1%
Chaos validation: synthetic network partition and node reboots executed in staging to validate rehydration and reconcilers
DR drill runbook exercise: quarterly scheduled drill with pre-approved blast radius and canary tenants, documented in Confluence
automation_tasks: Implement conductor lambda that sequences snapshot staging, fencing, rehydrate step, and traffic ramp (GH: PR #1792)
Add API endpoint for manual abort/force-promote with audit logging
Terraform: add DR policies and IAM roles for snapshot write/read in shared infra repo (PR #1546)
Integrate runbook gating with alertmanager webhook and Slack runbook channel to capture approvals
test_plan: Stage 1 - dry-run: execute conductor in a sandbox with synthetic data and no traffic (owner: QA)
Stage 2 - canary: promote a single non-critical cluster and route 3% traffic for 24 hours
Stage 3 - scheduled drill: full regional promotion during maintenance window with SRE oncall, validate rollback path
Stage 4 - post-drill: 72-hour watch with long-tail latency and error sampling

notes: Trade-offs: incremental snapshot rehydration reduces RPO but requires more complex reconciliation logic; chosen because customer-facing writes must be minimized during cutover.
Open questions: exact blast-radius for quarterly drills (need product input), consistent definition of 'non-critical' tenants for canary
Follow-ups: implement observability hooks to correlate conductor steps with tracing spans and add automated post-checks that publish results to the runbook channel
